question: What is the main job of the vascular system in our body?

options.B: Producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Transporting blood and nutrients to tissues
options.D: Filtering metabolic waste products from the kidneys

explanation: Think of the vascular system as the body's major highway network! It delivers fresh oxygen and vital nutrients to all our tissues while picking up waste along the way. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do we describe the vascular system as a "closed circuit"?

options.A: Valves prevent blood from flowing backward
options.B: Capillaries are sealed at both ends
options.C: Oxygen never leaves the blood plasma
options.D: Blood remains contained within vessels and the heart

explanation: You've got this! A "closed circuit" simply means blood travels inside a continuous, connected loop of the heart and blood vessels, rather than just floating freely in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which blood vessels act like tap controls to directly regulate blood flow into tiny capillary beds?
explanation: Arterioles are like the smart tap-taps of the circulatory system. Their muscular walls can tighten or relax to control exactly how much blood flows into local tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do the large arteries sitting right next to the heart need to be very stretchy and elastic?

options.A: To actively pump blood down to the lower limbs
options.B: To store extra blood volume during periods of rest
options.C: To allow white blood cells to squeeze through the walls
options.D: To absorb and cushion the pulsing pressure from the heart

explanation: Every time the heart pumps, it sends a strong wave of pressure. Stretchy arteries absorb that heavy surge so it doesn't damage smaller vessels downstream. Great job! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: What special structural feature makes capillary walls so great for exchanging nutrients and gases?

options.A: A single layer of endothelial cells

explanation: Capillaries are kept super thin—just one cell layer thick! This makes it very easy for oxygen and nutrients to slip quickly across to the cells that need them. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: Where in the body would you typically find special, highly permeable capillaries called sinusoids?
explanation: Sinusoids have larger gaps, acting like wide-open gates. You find them in busy filtering organs like the liver and spleen where whole cells and large molecules need to pass through easily. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: What clever feature stops blood in the leg veins from sliding backward against gravity?
explanation: Getting blood back up from your toes is hard work! Tiny one-way valves inside the veins act like little trapdoors, snapping shut to keep blood moving only toward the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h4)

question: How does our breathing (the respiratory pump) help push blood back up to the heart?

options.A: Lung expansion squeezes the aorta to raise pressure
options.B: Exhalation pushes air against the jugular veins
options.C: Deep breathing opens up the capillary sphincters
options.D: Inhalation creates chest pressure that draws blood upward

explanation: When you take a deep breath in, your chest cavity creates a gentle vacuum effect that draws blood upward from your abdomen and legs toward the heart. Nature's helper pump! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which layer of a blood vessel wall is mainly responsible for tightening to cause vasoconstriction?
explanation: The tunica media is the middle layer, packed with smooth muscle. When it contracts, the vessel narrows (vasoconstriction); when it relaxes, the vessel widens! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of the smooth inner lining (endothelium) in a blood vessel?

options.A: To reduce friction and prevent abnormal blood clotting
options.B: To pump blood forward without heart assistance
options.C: To store extra white blood cells during infection
options.D: To anchor the vessel securely to nearby bone

explanation: A slippery, smooth inner lining ensures blood glides smoothly without catching or forming accidental clots inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What naturally happens to a patient's blood pressure when their peripheral resistance goes up?
explanation: Imagine squeezing a garden hose narrower—the water pressure inside shoots up! The same rule applies: higher resistance in the blood vessels means higher blood pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: How do active body tissues locally manage to get more blood supply when they need it?

options.A: By sending nerve impulses directly to the heart valves
options.B: By releasing chemical factors that dilate local arterioles
options.C: By increasing the thickness of the tunica intima
options.D: By closing down all nearby capillary beds completely

explanation: When tissues work hard (like muscles during exercise), they release natural local signals (like CO2) telling nearby arterioles to relax and open wide for more blood flow. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main underlying process happening inside the arteries in atherosclerosis?

options.C: Dilation of superficial veins in the legs

explanation: Atherosclerosis happens when fatty deposits (plaques) gradually build up inside the arteries, making them narrower and stiffer over time. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which clinical problem is most directly caused by damaged, leaky venous valves in the legs?

options.B: Hemorrhagic stroke from a ruptured aneurysm
options.C: Acute myocardial infarction from coronary blockage
options.D: Sudden pulmonary embolism from air bubbles

explanation: If leg vein valves stop working well, blood starts to pool downward instead of flowing smoothly upward, leading to swelling, heaviness, and chronic venous insufficiency. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h7)
